```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY4", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch. UNBLIND is FALSE unless the environment variable
# UNBLIND_STUDY4 (a named setting the operating system passes to R) is set to
# TRUE. While it is FALSE, the labels are shuffled right after the data are
# built (section 3), and every output goes to a blind_run/ subfolder of the
# folder its real counterpart goes to. A value that is neither TRUE nor FALSE
# stops the run.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY4 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study4_01_Quant.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY4 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study4_01_Quant.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

# 0. What this file does

Study 4 asks whether what people are told about a first artwork, the source,
carries over to how they judge a second work that Alex makes from it. Two
things about the source vary. The label says that Alex made the source with
graphic design and sketching tools (Human) or by prompting an AI system that
generates the artworks (AI). The source time is the time Alex is said to have
spent on the source: less than 1 hour, 10 hours or 100 hours. Copyright in the
second work covers only what it adds to the source, so a rater who judges only
that addition should show neither the label nor the source time in their
ratings. Carry-over predicts both, largest when the second work is the source
unchanged.

The registration, `Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study4_AsPredicted.md`, is
the specification for everything below. Nothing this file computes beyond it
is presented as confirmatory.

**Design.** The label varies between participants: each sees one. The rest
varies within participants. Each participant sees 6 of the 10 sources, three
with a human or humanoid figure, two at each source time. Three second works
follow each source: None (the source unchanged), Slight (colour and contrast
adjustments) and Dramatic (substantial hand changes). Each second work is
rated on transformativeness, essence change and creativity, and each rating
is followed by a written justification, so each participant gives 54 ratings
and 54 justifications.

This file:

1. reads the two Qualtrics exports and the survey file, applies the registered
   exclusions in order, and checks every count the registration states
   (section 2);
2. scores each rating by its position on the answer scale and attaches the
   source time of each source (section 2);
3. shuffles the labels in a blind run and writes the long data file, one row
   per participant, second work and measure (section 3);
4. fits the registered model on each measure and runs the fifteen
   confirmatory tests with Holm's correction, which keeps the chance of any
   false positive among the fifteen at .05, and reads H1, H2 and H3 from
   them (sections 5 and 6);
5. checks each verdict with a cumulative-link model, a model that treats the
   answers as ordered categories (section 7);
6. runs the secondary analyses the registration names (section 8);
7. records the status of every fit and the run (sections 9 and 10).

The secondary refit that leaves out Human-arm participants who write that a
machine made the work needs the text measures, so it runs in
`Study4_03_Integration.Rmd`.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 fits the
# linear mixed models, regressions with an estimated adjustment for each
# participant and each source, and lmerTest adds F tests with Satterthwaite
# degrees of freedom, an approximation to the degrees of freedom a test in a
# mixed model has. emmeans gives estimated marginal means, the model's
# predicted mean for each level of a factor averaged over the other factors,
# and contrasts between them. ordinal fits the cumulative-link mixed models
# of section 7.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ordinal)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths and registered constants

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. Three environment variables override
# the defaults:
#   STUDY4_DIR           the Study 4 folder, where the outputs go
#   STUDY_SHARED_R       the folder of the shared R helpers
#   STUDY4_PROJECT_ROOT  the project root, the folder that holds Data and
#                        Analysis
# Printed paths are relative to the Study 4 folder or the project root, so no
# printed line names a folder particular to one machine.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY4_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R  <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R",
                        file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "qualtrics_import.R"))

PROJECT_ROOT <- find_project_root(start = STUDY_DIR,
                                  env_var = "STUDY4_PROJECT_ROOT")
EXPORTS <- study_export_paths(PROJECT_ROOT, 4)

# A blind run writes each file to a blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its
# real counterpart goes to.
mode_dir <- function(dir) if (UNBLIND) dir else file.path(dir, "blind_run")
OUT_STUDY  <- mode_dir(STUDY_DIR)
OUT_TABLES <- mode_dir(file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables"))
for (p in c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

cat("Mode:          ", if (UNBLIND) "unblinded" else "blind", "\n")
cat("Values export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$values, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Labels export: ", relative_path(EXPORTS$labels, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Survey file:   ", relative_path(EXPORTS$qsf, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Long data to:  ", relative_path(OUT_STUDY, STUDY_DIR), "\n")
cat("Tables to:     ", relative_path(OUT_TABLES, STUDY_DIR), "\n")

# The registered constants.
SEED         <- 20260421L  # the registered seed for R, used for every shuffle
EQ_BOUND     <- 0.224      # half the 0.448-point creativity penalty of Study 1
ALPHA        <- 0.05
N_FAMILY     <- 15L        # five confirmatory tests on each of three measures
MEASURES     <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
LABEL_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
TIME_LEVELS  <- c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")
MOD_LEVELS   <- c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")
SIX_POINT_ITEMS <- c("1NonFigureMinTrans", "1NonFigureNoneTrans")
TASK_ANSWER  <- "Viewing images for a set amount of time and answering questions"
# The two records registration question 6 names as failing the validity rule.
INVALID_RECORDS <- c("R_3SPOPWqijqK09xf", "R_6mZWuqtRNco0jiF")
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record ties every output to this run. It stores the SHA-256
# checksum of each input (a 64-character fingerprint of the file's exact
# bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest now, deletes each output's
# previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and writes the manifest last.
# A manifest on disk therefore means the run reached its end.
run <- start_run_record(
  c(values_export = EXPORTS$values,
    labels_export = EXPORTS$labels,
    survey_file   = EXPORTS$qsf),
  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_quant_run_manifest.csv"),
  STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_quant_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")
print(as.data.frame(run$inputs[, c("input", "file", "bytes", "sha256")]))

if (!UNBLIND) {
  # A short note in each blind folder says what the folder holds.
  blind_notes <- file.path(c(OUT_STUDY, OUT_TABLES), "BLIND_RUN.txt")
  run_clear_outputs(run, blind_notes)
  for (f in blind_notes) {
    writeLines(c(
      "Outputs of a blind run of the Study 4 pipeline.",
      "The Human and AI labels were shuffled across participants, the source",
      "times across each participant's six sources, and the modification levels",
      "across the three second works made from each source, before any summary",
      "or model. Study4_03_Integration.Rmd also shuffles the ratings across the",
      "responses to each question before it relates any word to a rating. No",
      "number in this folder describes the real conditions or the real link",
      "between the words and the ratings. A run with UNBLIND_STUDY4 set to TRUE",
      "writes the real outputs one folder up."), f)
  }
}
```

# 2. Import and exclusions

## 2.1 The exclusion flow

```{r exclusions}
# Qualtrics, the survey platform, exports the study twice: the Values export
# holds raw choice codes and the Labels export holds the text each
# participant saw. read_qualtrics_pair() reads both and checks that they hold
# the same records in the same order.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_exclusion_flow.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_validity_check.csv"))

ex <- read_qualtrics_pair(EXPORTS$values, EXPORTS$labels)
stopifnot(all(trim_answer(ex$labels$Status) %in% c("IP Address", "Survey Preview")))

# The 90 rating items and the source each belongs to. A source is one of the
# ten first artworks, named by its number and kind, such as 3NonFigure (the
# third source without a figure).
ITEMS <- rating_items(names(ex$values), "derivative")
ITEM_SOURCE <- sub("^(\\d(Figure|NonFigure)).*$", "\\1", ITEMS)
stopifnot(length(ITEMS) == 90, n_distinct(ITEM_SOURCE) == 10)

# The sources a record rated: those with an answer to at least one of their
# nine rating items.
rated_sources <- function(v) {
  answered <- vapply(ITEMS, function(item) trim_answer(v[[item]]) != "",
                     logical(nrow(v)))
  answered <- matrix(answered, nrow = nrow(v))
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(v)), function(i) sort(unique(ITEM_SOURCE[answered[i, ]])))
}

# The source named in each of the six image slots, Image1 to Image6, and the
# source time stated for it, Image1_Time to Image6_Time. A slot such as
# Image3_Nonfigure names the source 3NonFigure. A slot that names no source
# gives NA.
slot_table <- function(l) {
  bind_rows(lapply(1:6, function(k) {
    image <- trim_answer(l[[paste0("Image", k)]])
    parts <- regmatches(image, regexec("^Image([1-5])_(Figure|Nonfigure)$", image))
    tibble(row  = seq_len(nrow(l)),
           id   = l$ResponseId,
           slot = k,
           source = vapply(parts, function(p) {
             if (length(p) != 3) NA_character_
             else paste0(p[2], if (p[3] == "Figure") "Figure" else "NonFigure")
           }, character(1)),
           source_time = trim_answer(l[[paste0("Image", k, "_Time")]]))
  }))
}

# The validity rule of registration question 6. A valid completion rates
# exactly six sources, each named once in the six image slots, two per source
# time. One row per record, with the parts of the rule.
validity_table <- function(v, l) {
  slots <- slot_table(l)
  rated <- rated_sources(v)
  per_record <- slots %>%
    group_by(row) %>%
    summarise(
      n_slot_sources   = n_distinct(source[!is.na(source)]),
      any_slot_blank   = any(is.na(source)),
      sources_repeated = paste(sort(unique(source[duplicated(source) & !is.na(source)])),
                               collapse = " "),
      n_under_1  = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[1]),
      n_10       = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[2]),
      n_100      = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[3]),
      slot_set   = list(sort(unique(source[!is.na(source)]))),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(row)
  per_record %>%
    mutate(id = l$ResponseId,
           n_rated_sources = lengths(rated),
           rated_equals_slots = mapply(setequal, rated, slot_set),
           time_split = paste0(n_under_1, " at less than 1 hour, ", n_10,
                               " at 10 hours, ", n_100, " at 100 hours"),
           valid = n_rated_sources == 6 & n_slot_sources == 6 & !any_slot_blank &
             rated_equals_slots & n_under_1 == 2 & n_10 == 2 & n_100 == 2) %>%
    select(id, n_rated_sources, n_slot_sources, sources_repeated,
           rated_equals_slots, time_split, valid)
}

# The registered steps, in the order of registration question 6. Each step
# returns TRUE for the records it keeps. Survey Preview records are the
# survey's test runs. A blank seriousness answer counts as an answer other
# than "Yes, I did". A blank arithmetic answer passes.
steps <- list(
  "preview records, which are test runs (Status is Survey Preview)" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Status) == "IP Address",
  "unfinished records" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Finished) == "True",
  "any seriousness answer but Yes, I did, a blank included" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Seriousness) == "Yes, I did",
  "wrong answers to What does 8+7 equal? (a blank passes)" =
    function(v, l) {
      a <- trim_answer(l$AttentionCheck2)
      a == "" | a == "15"
    },
  "records that are not a valid completion" =
    function(v, l) validity_table(v, l)$valid
)
flow <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps)

# One line per step, so the flow can be read off the report.
ff <- flow$flow
cat("Records in the export:", ff$n[1], "\n")
for (i in 2:nrow(ff)) {
  cat(sprintf("Step %d, %s: %d -> %d (%d removed)\n",
              i - 1, ff$step[i], ff$n[i - 1], ff$n[i], ff$removed[i]))
}

# The counts the registration states. The run stops if the exports give
# anything else.
REGISTERED_FLOW <- c(140L, 133L, 125L, 119L, 119L, 117L)
ff$registered_n <- REGISTERED_FLOW
ff$match <- ff$n == ff$registered_n
if (!identical(as.integer(ff$n), REGISTERED_FLOW)) {
  stop("The exclusion flow does not match the registration: ",
       paste(ff$n, collapse = " -> "), " against ",
       paste(REGISTERED_FLOW, collapse = " -> "), ".")
}
write_csv(ff, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_exclusion_flow.csv"))

# The 119 records left after the arithmetic step. The registration states
# that none answered the arithmetic question wrongly, that all have a
# recorded condition and that all answered the task question correctly.
after4 <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps[1:4])
arith  <- trim_answer(after4$labels$AttentionCheck2)
cat("Blank arithmetic answers that passed:", sum(arith == ""), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(after4$labels) == 119,
          all(trim_answer(after4$labels$Type) %in% LABEL_LEVELS),
          all(trim_answer(after4$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER))
cat("Of the 119, with a condition:",
    sum(trim_answer(after4$labels$Type) %in% LABEL_LEVELS),
    "| with the correct task answer:",
    sum(trim_answer(after4$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER), "\n")

# The validity rule removes exactly the two records the registration names.
validity <- validity_table(after4$values, after4$labels)
failing  <- validity %>% filter(!valid) %>%
  mutate(reason = case_when(
    n_rated_sources != 6 ~ paste0("rated ", n_rated_sources, " sources"),
    sources_repeated != "" ~ paste0("names ", sources_repeated,
                                    " in two slots; source times ", time_split),
    TRUE ~ "other")) %>%
  arrange(id)
print(as.data.frame(failing))
stopifnot(setequal(failing$id, INVALID_RECORDS), !any(failing$reason == "other"))
write_csv(failing, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_validity_check.csv"))

# The arms of the 117 participants the registration analyses.
arms <- table(factor(trim_answer(flow$labels$Type), levels = LABEL_LEVELS))
print(arms)
stopifnot(arms[["AI"]] == 62, arms[["Human"]] == 55)
```

## 2.2 Scoring by position

```{r scoring}
# Each rating is scored 1 to k by the position of its label among the item's
# answer options, read from the survey file in the order they were shown,
# because the numeric export stores raw choice codes, not scale positions.
# An answer whose label is not among the item's options would be scored NA
# and listed; none is.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_item_scales.csv"))

scales <- read_item_scales(EXPORTS$qsf, ITEM_FAMILIES$derivative$pattern)
cat("Rating items:", nrow(scales), "| five-point:", sum(scales$k == 5),
    "| six-point:", sum(scales$k == 6), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(scales) == 90, sum(scales$k == 5) == 88,
          setequal(scales$item[scales$k == 6], SIX_POINT_ITEMS))
write_csv(select(scales, item, question_id, k, anchors, stem),
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_item_scales.csv"))

# Registration question 8 names wording slips in three essence items' answer
# options and one reworded creativity stem. Each item is scored against its
# own options, so a slip changes no score. The option sets and stems, with
# the number of items carrying each:
scale_parts <- parse_item_names(scales$item, "derivative") %>%
  select(item, dimension) %>%
  left_join(select(scales, item, anchors, stem), by = "item")
print(as.data.frame(count(scale_parts, dimension, anchors)))
print(as.data.frame(count(scale_parts, dimension, stem) %>%
                      mutate(stem = substr(stem, 1, 70))))

built <- reshape_ratings_long(flow$values, flow$labels, scales, "derivative",
                              carry_labels = "Type")
cat("Answers that could not be scored:", nrow(built$unscored), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(built$unscored) == 0)
```

## 2.3 The source time of each source

```{r source-times}
# The survey records the source shown in each of the six slots and the
# source time stated for it. These slot fields are the only record of which
# source carried which time; the export's single ArtistHr field holds one
# time per record, not one per source, and is not used.
image_slots <- slot_table(flow$labels) %>% select(id, slot, source, source_time)
if (anyNA(image_slots$source)) stop("Some image slot names no source.")
if (!all(image_slots$source_time %in% TIME_LEVELS)) {
  stop("Some source time is not one of the three registered times.")
}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(image_slots[, c("id", "source")]))

# Each participant saw six different sources, three with a figure, two at
# each source time.
per_person_slots <- image_slots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_sources = n_distinct(source),
            n_figure  = sum(grepl("[0-9]Figure$", source)),
            n_under_1 = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[1]),
            n_10      = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[2]),
            n_100     = sum(source_time == TIME_LEVELS[3]), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(per_person_slots) == 117, all(per_person_slots$n_sources == 6),
          all(per_person_slots$n_figure == 3), all(per_person_slots$n_under_1 == 2),
          all(per_person_slots$n_10 == 2), all(per_person_slots$n_100 == 2))
cat("Every participant saw 6 sources, 3 with a figure, 2 at each source time.\n")
```

## 2.4 The long data and the registered counts

```{r long-data}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_sample_checks.csv"))

# One row per participant, second work and measure. A second work is one
# source at one modification level, named by work_id, such as 3NonFigure_Slight.
# The source time comes from the source's slot, and every rated source must
# be one of the six the slots name.
long <- built$long %>%
  left_join(rename(select(image_slots, id, source, source_time),
                   stimulus_id = source),
            by = c("id", "stimulus_id"), relationship = "many-to-one")
if (anyNA(long$source_time)) stop("Some rated source is not among the six listed.")

long <- long %>%
  transmute(id,
            label       = Type,
            source      = stimulus_id,
            image_kind  = stimulus_type,
            source_time,
            modification,
            work_id     = paste0(stimulus_id, "_", modification),
            dimension, item, k_points, rating, rating_label,
            response_text = justification)

# The design within each participant: 6 sources, each at the three
# modification levels, 18 second works, 54 ratings and 54 justifications.
per_person <- long %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_rows      = n(),
            n_works     = n_distinct(work_id),
            n_ratings   = sum(!is.na(rating)),
            n_justified = sum(response_text != ""), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(per_person$n_rows == 54), all(per_person$n_works == 18),
          all(per_person$n_ratings == 54), all(per_person$n_justified == 54))
works_per_source <- long %>% distinct(id, source, modification) %>% count(id, source)
stopifnot(all(works_per_source$n == 3))

# The counts the registration states, beside the counts the data give.
participants <- distinct(long, id, label)
sample_checks <- tribble(
  ~quantity,                                          ~registered, ~observed,
  "participants analysed",                            117L, nrow(participants),
  "participants in the AI arm",                       62L,  sum(participants$label == "AI"),
  "participants in the Human arm",                    55L,  sum(participants$label == "Human"),
  "justifications",                                   6318L, sum(long$response_text != ""),
  "ratings on the two six-point items, left out",     140L, sum(long$k_points == 6 & !is.na(long$rating)),
  "analysed ratings",                                 6178L, sum(long$k_points == 5 & !is.na(long$rating))
) %>% mutate(match = registered == observed)
print(as.data.frame(sample_checks))
write_csv(sample_checks, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_sample_checks.csv"))
if (!all(sample_checks$match)) stop("The sample does not match the registration.")
stopifnot(nrow(long) == 117 * 54)
```

# 3. The blind shuffle and the long data file

```{r blind-shuffle}
# In a blind run the labels are shuffled here, after the data are built and
# before any summary or model. Three labels are shuffled.
#
# The Human and AI label is between participants. blind_shuffle() deals each
# participant another participant's label, so each arm keeps its 62 or 55
# participants.
#
# Source time varies within each participant across sources. The
# participant's six source times are dealt again among the same six sources,
# each source keeping one time for all its ratings, so every participant keeps
# two sources at each time.
#
# Modification varies within each source across its three second works. The
# three levels are dealt again among the three second works of each
# participant and source, each work keeping one level for its three ratings.
# The work_id column still names the second work the participant saw and
# wrote about, because it keys the text tables; the modification column is
# the one the models read.
#
# Every shuffle uses the registered seed, takes participants and units in
# byte order of their identifiers so that the result is the same on every
# machine, and puts the random-number state back afterwards.
shuffle_within <- function(df, group_cols, unit_col, label_col, seed) {
  units <- distinct(df[, c(group_cols, unit_col, label_col)])
  if (anyDuplicated(units[, c(group_cols, unit_col)]) > 0) {
    stop("Some ", unit_col, " carries more than one ", label_col, ".")
  }
  group_key <- do.call(paste, c(units[group_cols], sep = "\r"))
  units <- units[order(group_key, units[[unit_col]], method = "radix"), ]
  group_key <- do.call(paste, c(units[group_cols], sep = "\r"))
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  rows_by_group <- split(seq_len(nrow(units)),
                         factor(group_key, levels = unique(group_key)))
  dealt <- character(nrow(units))
  for (rows in rows_by_group) {
    dealt[rows] <- units[[label_col]][rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  out <- df
  key_df    <- do.call(paste, c(df[c(group_cols, unit_col)], sep = "\r"))
  key_units <- do.call(paste, c(units[c(group_cols, unit_col)], sep = "\r"))
  out[[label_col]] <- dealt[match(key_df, key_units)]
  out
}

design_counts <- function(d) {
  list(arms  = table(distinct(d, id, label)$label),
       times = table(distinct(d, id, source, source_time)[, c("id", "source_time")]),
       mods  = table(distinct(d, id, source, work_id, modification)[, c("id", "source", "modification")]))
}

if (!UNBLIND) {
  before <- design_counts(long)
  long <- blind_shuffle(long, "id", "label", seed = SEED)
  long <- shuffle_within(long, "id", "source", "source_time", seed = SEED)
  long <- shuffle_within(long, c("id", "source"), "work_id", "modification", seed = SEED)
  after <- design_counts(long)
  # The design survives the shuffles: 62 and 55 participants, two sources at
  # each time for every participant, one second work at each level for every
  # source.
  stopifnot(identical(before$arms, after$arms),
            all(after$times == 2),
            all(after$mods[after$mods > 0] == 1),
            sum(after$mods) == 117 * 18)
  cat("Blind run: labels shuffled across participants, source times within",
      "each participant, modification levels within each source; seed", SEED, "\n")
}
long$label_mode <- if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled"

long <- long %>%
  mutate(label        = factor(label, levels = LABEL_LEVELS),
         source_time  = factor(source_time, levels = TIME_LEVELS),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
         dimension    = factor(dimension, levels = MEASURES)) %>%
  arrange(id, work_id, dimension)
stopifnot(!anyNA(long$label), !anyNA(long$source_time),
          !anyNA(long$modification), !anyNA(long$dimension))
```

# 5. The registered models

```{r fit-models}
# Each measure gets a linear mixed model, a regression with an estimated
# adjustment for each participant and each source:
#
#   rating ~ label x source time x modification + (1 | participant) + (1 | source)
#
# with no term for whether the source shows a figure. The six-point
# transformativeness items are left out, so every analysed rating is on five
# points. Every factor uses sum-to-zero contrasts, a coding in which a
# factor's effects add to zero across its levels, so that each main effect is
# averaged over the other factors. The fit is by restricted maximum
# likelihood (REML, the usual estimator of the variances in a mixed model)
# with the bobyqa optimizer, the routine that searches for the best-fitting
# values, as in Study 1. fit_with_status() keeps every
# warning and records whether the fit converged and whether it is singular
# (a variance estimated at zero).
SUM_CONTRASTS <- list(label = "contr.sum", source_time = "contr.sum",
                      modification = "contr.sum")
FIXED_RHS <- ~ label * source_time * modification
FORMULA   <- rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source)
FORMULA_TEXT <- "rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source)"

model_data <- function(m) {
  long %>%
    filter(dimension == m, k_points == 5, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(id = factor(id), source = factor(source))
}
fit_registered <- function(d) {
  res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
    FORMULA, data = d, REML = TRUE, contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
  res$data <- d
  res
}

data_by_measure <- setNames(lapply(MEASURES, model_data), MEASURES)
stopifnot(sum(vapply(data_by_measure, nrow, integer(1))) == 6178)
primary <- lapply(data_by_measure, fit_registered)
for (m in MEASURES) {
  st <- primary[[m]]$status
  cat(sprintf("%-18s rows %4d | fit error %s | converged %s | singular %s\n",
              m, nrow(data_by_measure[[m]]), st$fit_error, st$converged, st$singular))
}
```

# 6. The fifteen confirmatory tests

## 6.1 The tests and the Holm family

```{r confirmatory}
# Five tests on each measure, fifteen in all:
#
#   1. Slight minus None, averaged over label and source time;
#   2. Dramatic minus Slight, averaged the same way;
#   3. Human minus AI, averaged over source time and modification, by an
#      equivalence test against plus or minus 0.224 rating points;
#   4. source time, an F test averaged over the other factors;
#   5. source time by modification, an F test.
#
# Tests 1 and 2 are contrasts between estimated marginal means, each with a
# two-sided t test. Test 3 is two one-sided tests: one asks whether the
# difference lies above -0.224, the other whether it lies below +0.224, and
# both pass exactly when the 90 percent confidence interval lies inside the
# bound. The larger of the two one-sided p-values is the test's p-value.
# Tests 4 and 5 come from the type III table, in which each term is tested
# with every other term in the model. Degrees of freedom are Satterthwaite's
# throughout.
#
# Holm's method corrects the fifteen together: the p-values are ordered, the
# smallest is compared with .05 divided by fifteen, the next with .05 divided
# by fourteen, and so on, stopping at the first that fails. This holds the
# chance of any false positive among the fifteen at .05. The correction is
# told the family has fifteen members whatever happens, so a missing p-value
# never makes it lighter for the others.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_lmm_anova.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_confirmatory_family.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_hypotheses.csv"))

# emmeans switches off Satterthwaite degrees of freedom above 3,000
# observations unless told otherwise. The registration names them, so the
# limit is raised above the size of any model here.
emm_of <- function(res, spec) {
  emmeans::emmeans(res$fit, specs = spec, data = res$data,
                   lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 20000)
}

# Two one-sided tests of an estimate against plus or minus a bound.
tost <- function(est, se, df, bound, alpha = ALPHA) {
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  tibble(ci90_low = est - crit * se, ci90_high = est + crit * se,
         p_lower = p_lower, p_upper = p_upper, tost_p = pmax(p_lower, p_upper))
}

MOD_CONTRASTS <- list("Slight minus None"     = c(-1, 1, 0),
                      "Dramatic minus Slight" = c(0, -1, 1))
TEST_NAMES <- c("Slight minus None",
                "Dramatic minus Slight",
                "Human minus AI, equivalence within plus or minus 0.224",
                "source time",
                "source time by modification")

anova_rows <- function(res, m) {
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) {
    return(tibble(measure = m, term = NA_character_, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  a <- as.data.frame(anova(res$fit, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
  tibble(measure = m, term = rownames(a), num_df = a$NumDF, den_df = a$DenDF,
         F = a[["F value"]], p = na_unless_usable(a[["Pr(>F)"]], res$status),
         converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
         note = fit_note(res$status))
}

family_rows <- function(res, m) {
  base <- tibble(measure = m, test_number = 1:5, test = TEST_NAMES,
                 hypothesis = c("H1", "H1", "H2", "H3", "H3"),
                 kind = c("contrast, two-sided t test", "contrast, two-sided t test",
                          "equivalence, two one-sided t tests", "F test", "F test"),
                 converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
                 note = fit_note(res$status))
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) return(base)
  mc <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res, ~ modification),
                                            MOD_CONTRASTS, adjust = "none"),
                          infer = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  lc <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res, ~ label),
                                            list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)),
                                            adjust = "none"),
                          infer = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  eq <- tost(lc$estimate, lc$SE, lc$df, EQ_BOUND)
  # emmeans gives the same equivalence p-value through its own test.
  eq_emm <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::test(
    emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res, ~ label), list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1))),
    delta = EQ_BOUND, side = "equivalence")))$p.value
  stopifnot(abs(eq_emm - eq$tost_p) < 1e-8)
  a <- as.data.frame(anova(res$fit, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
  f_terms <- c("source_time", "source_time:modification")
  base %>% mutate(
    term      = c("modification", "modification", "label", f_terms),
    estimate  = c(mc$estimate, lc$estimate, NA, NA),
    std_error = c(mc$SE, lc$SE, NA, NA),
    statistic = c(mc$t.ratio, lc$t.ratio, a[f_terms, "F value"]),
    num_df    = c(NA, NA, NA, a[f_terms, "NumDF"]),
    den_df    = c(mc$df, lc$df, a[f_terms, "DenDF"]),
    ci90_low  = c(NA, NA, eq$ci90_low, NA, NA),
    ci90_high = c(NA, NA, eq$ci90_high, NA, NA),
    p_lower   = c(NA, NA, eq$p_lower, NA, NA),
    p_upper   = c(NA, NA, eq$p_upper, NA, NA),
    p_raw     = na_unless_usable(c(mc$p.value, eq$tost_p, a[f_terms, "Pr(>F)"]),
                                 res$status),
    ci90_inside_bound = na_unless_usable(
      c(NA, NA, eq$ci90_low > -EQ_BOUND & eq$ci90_high < EQ_BOUND, NA, NA),
      res$status))
}

lmm_anova <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) anova_rows(primary[[m]], m)))
write_csv(lmm_anova, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_lmm_anova.csv"))

confirmatory <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) family_rows(primary[[m]], m))) %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = N_FAMILY),
         holm_significant = p_holm < ALPHA,
         bound = ifelse(test_number == 3, EQ_BOUND, NA_real_),
         family = "fifteen registered tests, five per measure, Holm, family-wise alpha .05",
         model = paste0(FORMULA_TEXT, ", sum-to-zero contrasts, REML, bobyqa; ",
                        "Satterthwaite degrees of freedom")) %>%
  relocate(p_holm, holm_significant, .after = p_raw) %>%
  relocate(converged, singular, note, .after = bound)
stopifnot(nrow(confirmatory) == N_FAMILY,
          all((confirmatory$p_raw[confirmatory$test_number == 3] < ALPHA) ==
                confirmatory$ci90_inside_bound[confirmatory$test_number == 3],
              na.rm = TRUE))
write_csv(confirmatory, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_confirmatory_family.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(confirmatory %>%
                      select(measure, test, estimate, statistic, den_df, p_raw,
                             p_holm, holm_significant) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

## 6.2 The registered reading of each hypothesis

```{r hypotheses}
# H1 holds on a measure when Slight minus None and Dramatic minus Slight are
# both positive and both survive the Holm correction. H2 holds on a measure
# when the equivalence test of Human minus AI survives the Holm correction,
# so that the label's average effect lies inside plus or minus 0.224. H3 has
# no predicted direction, and its two F tests are read as surviving the
# correction or not. A measure whose fit is not usable gets no verdict. The
# table has one row per measure and hypothesis reading, and two more for H1
# and H2 over all three measures.
hypotheses <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  f <- confirmatory %>% filter(measure == m)
  usable <- fit_usable(primary[[m]]$status)
  t1 <- f[f$test_number == 1, ]; t2 <- f[f$test_number == 2, ]
  t3 <- f[f$test_number == 3, ]; t4 <- f[f$test_number == 4, ]
  t5 <- f[f$test_number == 5, ]
  h1_met <- t1$estimate > 0 & t1$holm_significant & t2$estimate > 0 & t2$holm_significant
  tibble(
    measure = m,
    hypothesis = c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H3"),
    test = c("Slight minus None and Dramatic minus Slight", TEST_NAMES[3],
             TEST_NAMES[4], TEST_NAMES[5]),
    requirement = c(
      "both contrasts positive and significant after Holm",
      "equivalence p-value below .05 after Holm",
      "no predicted direction; significant after Holm or not",
      "no predicted direction; significant after Holm or not"),
    verdict = if (!usable) NA_character_ else c(
      if (h1_met) "supported" else "not supported",
      if (t3$holm_significant) "inside the bound" else "not shown inside the bound",
      if (t4$holm_significant) "significant after Holm" else "not significant after Holm",
      if (t5$holm_significant) "significant after Holm" else "not significant after Holm"),
    note = fit_note(primary[[m]]$status, what = "verdict"))
}))

# The registration states H1 and H2 for every measure, so each also gets one
# reading over the three measures. It holds when it holds on all three, it
# fails when it fails on any one, and it has no reading while some measure
# has no verdict.
across_measures <- function(h, test, met, holds, fails) {
  v <- hypotheses$verdict[hypotheses$hypothesis == h]
  stopifnot(length(v) == length(MEASURES))
  tibble(measure = "all three measures", hypothesis = h, test = test,
         requirement = paste0(met, " on each of the three measures"),
         verdict = if (anyNA(v)) NA_character_ else if (all(v == met)) holds else fails,
         note = if (anyNA(v)) "some measure has no verdict, so this reading is NA" else "")
}
hypotheses <- bind_rows(
  hypotheses,
  across_measures("H1", "Slight minus None and Dramatic minus Slight", "supported",
                  "supported", "not supported"),
  across_measures("H2", TEST_NAMES[3], "inside the bound",
                  "inside the bound", "not shown inside the bound"))
stopifnot(nrow(hypotheses) == 4 * length(MEASURES) + 2)
write_csv(hypotheses, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_hypotheses.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(hypotheses, measure, hypothesis, test, verdict)))
```

## 6.3 Estimated marginal means

```{r emmeans}
# From each fit: the predicted mean of every cell of label, source time and
# modification, and the predicted mean of each level of each factor averaged
# over the other two, with 95 percent confidence intervals.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_emmeans_cells.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_emmeans_marginal.csv"))

emm_frame <- function(res, m, spec) {
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) {
    return(tibble(measure = m, note = fit_note(res$status, "mean")))
  }
  as_tibble(summary(emm_of(res, spec))) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    rename(std_error = SE, ci95_low = lower.CL, ci95_high = upper.CL) %>%
    mutate(measure = m, .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(note = "")
}
emm_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  emm_frame(primary[[m]], m, ~ label * source_time * modification)
}))
emm_marginal <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("label", "source_time", "modification"), function(f) {
    emm_frame(primary[[m]], m, as.formula(paste("~", f))) %>%
      rename(level = all_of(f)) %>%
      mutate(factor = f, .after = measure)
  }))
}))
stopifnot(nrow(emm_cells) == 3 * 18, nrow(emm_marginal) == 3 * 8)
write_csv(emm_cells, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_emmeans_cells.csv"))
write_csv(emm_marginal, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_emmeans_marginal.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(emm_marginal %>% select(measure, factor, level, emmean, ci95_low,
                                            ci95_high) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

# 7. The cumulative-link check of each verdict

```{r clmm}
# A cumulative-link mixed model treats the five answers as ordered
# categories: it estimates where the cut points between neighbouring answers
# fall on an underlying scale instead of treating the answers as evenly
# spaced numbers. Each measure's registered model is refitted in that form,
# with the logit link (a logistic curve for the chance of answering above
# each cut point), the same fixed and random terms and the same sum-to-zero
# contrasts, by the Laplace approximation (the ordinal package's default way
# of averaging over the participant and source adjustments):
#
#   ordered rating ~ label x source time x modification + (1 | participant) + (1 | source)
#
# Tests 1 and 2 become Wald z tests of the same contrasts on the underlying
# scale (the contrast divided by its standard error, compared with a normal
# distribution). Tests 4 and 5 become Wald chi-square tests of the same
# terms (the squared estimates weighed against their covariance, compared
# with a chi-square distribution). Test 3 has no counterpart: its bound is in
# rating points, and the underlying scale has no rating points, so it is not
# checked. The twelve p-values are corrected by Holm as members of the
# registered family of fifteen, so the correction is no lighter than the
# linear model's, and each verdict is set beside the linear model's.
#
# A fit counts as converged when the optimizer returns code 0 and raises no
# warning about convergence or the Hessian (the matrix of second derivatives
# the standard errors come from), as in Study 1. It counts as singular when a
# random-effect standard deviation lies below 1e-4.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_clmm_check.csv"))

fit_clmm <- function(d) {
  d$rating_ord <- factor(d$rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE)
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(rating_ord ~ label * source_time * modification +
                             (1 | id) + (1 | source),
                           data = d, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE,
                           contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  status <- tibble(
    fit_error = failed,
    converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
      !any(grepl("converge|Hessian", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
    singular  = if (failed) NA else
      any(vapply(ordinal::VarCorr(fit), function(m) any(attr(m, "stddev") < 1e-4),
                 logical(1))),
    lme4_messages = paste(unique(c(if (failed) conditionMessage(fit), warns)),
                          collapse = " | "))
  list(fit = fit, data = d, status = status,
       max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)))
}

# The contrasts of tests 1 and 2 as weights on the fixed effects. Each level's
# mean is the average of the model's rows for the 18 cells at that level,
# which with sum-to-zero contrasts averages over label and source time with
# equal weights, as emmeans does.
grid <- expand.grid(label = factor(LABEL_LEVELS, LABEL_LEVELS),
                    source_time = factor(TIME_LEVELS, TIME_LEVELS),
                    modification = factor(MOD_LEVELS, MOD_LEVELS))
X_grid <- model.matrix(FIXED_RHS, grid, contrasts.arg = SUM_CONTRASTS)
level_row <- function(level) colMeans(X_grid[grid$modification == level, , drop = FALSE])
L_CONTRASTS <- list(
  "Slight minus None"     = (level_row("Slight") - level_row("None"))[-1],
  "Dramatic minus Slight" = (level_row("Dramatic") - level_row("Slight"))[-1])
TERM_ASSIGN <- attr(X_grid, "assign")[-1]
TERM_LABELS <- attr(terms(FIXED_RHS), "term.labels")

# The same weights applied to each linear model's fixed effects reproduce the
# emmeans contrasts of section 6, which shows the weights are right.
for (m in MEASURES) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) next
  b <- lme4::fixef(res$fit)[-1]
  stopifnot(identical(names(b), names(L_CONTRASTS[[1]])))
  est <- vapply(L_CONTRASTS, function(L) sum(L * b), numeric(1))
  ref <- confirmatory %>% filter(measure == m, test_number %in% 1:2)
  stopifnot(max(abs(est - ref$estimate)) < 1e-8)
}

clmm_wald <- function(cl) {
  beta <- cl$fit$beta
  stopifnot(identical(names(beta), names(L_CONTRASTS[[1]])))
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(cl$fit))[names(beta), names(beta)]
  contrast_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(names(L_CONTRASTS), function(nm) {
    L <- L_CONTRASTS[[nm]]
    est <- sum(L * beta)
    se  <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(L) %*% V %*% L))
    tibble(test = nm, clmm_estimate = est, clmm_statistic = est / se, clmm_df = 1L,
           clmm_p_raw = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)))
  }))
  term_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(c("source_time", "source_time:modification"), function(term) {
    idx <- which(TERM_ASSIGN == match(term, TERM_LABELS))
    b <- beta[idx]
    w <- as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V[idx, idx, drop = FALSE], b))
    tibble(test = TEST_NAMES[match(term, c("source_time", "source_time:modification")) + 3],
           clmm_estimate = NA_real_, clmm_statistic = w, clmm_df = length(idx),
           clmm_p_raw = pchisq(w, length(idx), lower.tail = FALSE))
  }))
  bind_rows(contrast_rows, term_rows)
}

clmm_fits <- lapply(data_by_measure, fit_clmm)
clmm_check <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[m]]
  usable <- fit_usable(cl$status)
  w <- if (isTRUE(cl$status$fit_error)) {
    tibble(test = TEST_NAMES[c(1, 2, 4, 5)], clmm_estimate = NA_real_,
           clmm_statistic = NA_real_, clmm_df = NA_integer_, clmm_p_raw = NA_real_)
  } else clmm_wald(cl)
  w %>% mutate(measure = m, .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(clmm_p_raw = if (usable) clmm_p_raw else NA_real_,
           clmm_converged = cl$status$converged,
           clmm_singular  = cl$status$singular,
           max_abs_gradient = cl$max_abs_gradient,
           note = fit_note(cl$status))
})) %>%
  mutate(clmm_p_holm = p.adjust(clmm_p_raw, method = "holm", n = N_FAMILY),
         clmm_holm_significant = clmm_p_holm < ALPHA) %>%
  left_join(confirmatory %>% select(measure, test, test_number, lmm_estimate = estimate,
                                    lmm_p_holm = p_holm,
                                    lmm_holm_significant = holm_significant),
            by = c("measure", "test")) %>%
  mutate(same_direction = ifelse(test_number %in% 1:2,
                                 sign(clmm_estimate) == sign(lmm_estimate), NA),
         verdicts_agree = clmm_holm_significant == lmm_holm_significant &
           (is.na(same_direction) | same_direction),
         model = "ordered rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source), logit link, Laplace approximation, sum-to-zero contrasts; Wald tests") %>%
  relocate(test_number, .after = measure) %>%
  arrange(measure, test_number)
stopifnot(nrow(clmm_check) == 12)
write_csv(clmm_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_clmm_check.csv"))
for (m in MEASURES) {
  cl <- clmm_fits[[m]]
  cat(sprintf("%-18s cumulative-link fit: fit error %s | converged %s | singular %s | largest absolute gradient %s\n",
              m, cl$status$fit_error, cl$status$converged, cl$status$singular,
              signif(cl$max_abs_gradient, 3)))
}
print(as.data.frame(clmm_check %>%
                      select(measure, test, clmm_p_holm, clmm_holm_significant,
                             lmm_holm_significant, verdicts_agree) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

# 8. Secondary analyses

```{r secondary}
# Registration question 8 names three secondary analyses. None enters the
# Holm family, and no p-value here is corrected.
#
#   (a) The label effect at each modification level: Human minus AI at None,
#       Slight and Dramatic, averaged over source time, with its 95 percent
#       interval and two-sided test, and its equivalence test against the
#       same bound of plus or minus 0.224.
#   (b) Whether source time changes the label effect: the label by source
#       time F test from the type III table, and Human minus AI at each
#       source time, averaged over modification.
#   (c) Whether 100 hours and less than 1 hour are equivalent: the contrast
#       averaged over label and modification, with its equivalence test
#       against the same bound.
#
# The fourth secondary analysis, the refit without Human-arm participants who
# write that a machine made the work, runs in Study4_03_Integration.Rmd.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_label_by_modification.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_label_by_source_time.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_time_equivalence.csv"))

contrast_table <- function(res, m, spec, weights) {
  ct <- emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res, spec), weights, adjust = "none")
  as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    rename(std_error = SE, ci95_low = lower.CL, ci95_high = upper.CL,
           t = t.ratio, p_two_sided = p.value) %>%
    mutate(measure = m, .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(across(c(ci95_low, ci95_high, p_two_sided),
                  ~ na_unless_usable(.x, res$status)))
}
with_tost <- function(tab, res) {
  eq <- tost(tab$estimate, tab$std_error, tab$df, EQ_BOUND)
  tab %>% mutate(bound = EQ_BOUND,
                 ci90_low = na_unless_usable(eq$ci90_low, res$status),
                 ci90_high = na_unless_usable(eq$ci90_high, res$status),
                 tost_p = na_unless_usable(eq$tost_p, res$status),
                 inside_bound = tost_p < ALPHA)
}

label_by_mod <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) return(tibble(measure = m, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  contrast_table(res, m, ~ label | modification, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1))) %>%
    with_tost(res) %>%
    mutate(averaged_over = "source time, equal weights", correction = "none", note = "")
}))

label_by_time <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) return(tibble(measure = m, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  f <- lmm_anova %>% filter(measure == m, term == "label:source_time")
  contrast_table(res, m, ~ label | source_time, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1))) %>%
    mutate(averaged_over = "modification, equal weights",
           interaction_F = f$F, interaction_num_df = f$num_df,
           interaction_den_df = f$den_df, interaction_p = f$p,
           correction = "none", note = "")
}))

time_equivalence <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  res <- primary[[m]]
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) return(tibble(measure = m, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  contrast_table(res, m, ~ source_time,
                 list("100 hours minus less than 1 hour" = c(-1, 0, 1))) %>%
    with_tost(res) %>%
    mutate(averaged_over = "label and modification, equal weights",
           correction = "none", note = "")
}))

stopifnot(nrow(label_by_mod) == 9, nrow(label_by_time) == 9, nrow(time_equivalence) == 3)
write_csv(label_by_mod, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_label_by_modification.csv"))
write_csv(label_by_time, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_label_by_source_time.csv"))
write_csv(time_equivalence, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_time_equivalence.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(label_by_mod %>% select(measure, modification, estimate, ci95_low,
                                            ci95_high, tost_p, inside_bound) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
print(as.data.frame(label_by_time %>% select(measure, source_time, estimate, ci95_low,
                                             ci95_high, interaction_p) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
print(as.data.frame(time_equivalence %>% select(measure, estimate, ci90_low, ci90_high,
                                                tost_p, inside_bound) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

# 9. Fit status

```{r fit-status}
# One row per fit in this file: the registered model and the cumulative-link
# model, on each measure. A fit is usable when it did not stop with an error
# and converged; a singular fit that converged keeps its numbers.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_fit_status.csv"))
status_row <- function(status, m, role, formula, d) {
  status %>%
    select(fit_error, converged, singular, lme4_messages) %>%
    mutate(measure = m, role = role, model = formula, n_obs = nrow(d),
           n_participants = n_distinct(d$id), n_sources = n_distinct(d$source),
           usable = fit_usable(status), .before = 1)
}
fit_status <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(
    status_row(primary[[m]]$status, m, "registered model", FORMULA_TEXT,
               data_by_measure[[m]]),
    status_row(clmm_fits[[m]]$status, m, "cumulative-link check",
               "ordered rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source)",
               data_by_measure[[m]]))
}))
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_status, measure, role, n_obs, usable, fit_error,
                           converged, singular)))
write_csv(fit_status, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_fit_status.csv"))
cat("Linear mixed models converged:",
    sum(fit_status$converged[fit_status$role == "registered model"]), "of 3 | singular:",
    sum(fit_status$singular[fit_status$role == "registered model"] %in% TRUE), "\n")
cat("Cumulative-link models converged:",
    sum(fit_status$converged[fit_status$role == "cumulative-link check"]), "of 3 | singular:",
    sum(fit_status$singular[fit_status$role == "cumulative-link check"] %in% TRUE), "\n")
```
